svg.aria-label: How to write ਮਨਨ: 7 strokes · 6 pen lifts · 12 movements
svg.title: Writing ਮਨਨ
svg.desc: 12 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ਮਨਨ (gurmukhi): each letter's body in reading order, then one headline over the whole word; the movement being added is drawn in ink over the finished word, whose outline (each letter's at the font's advance) is read from _fonts/NotoSansGurmukhi-Static.ttf. Stroke order after letter 1: GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਮ (mammaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–2 (lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart line 952, commit de1e560; Apache-2.0); letters 2 and 3: GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਨ (nannaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–4 (lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart line 785, commit de1e560; Apache-2.0); the shared headline, drawn last: by this book's convention for words, not from a Gurmukhi recording: the order fluent writers are described as using, and the one this book draws Devanagari words in, after HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit 4.0 Devanagari pen data (headline last in 82% of 2,706 consonant prototypes); GNPS's own letters draw the headline first <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>. Source note on variation: The letters are drawn in reading order, each as its own cited strip draws it but without its own headline, placed where the bundled font prints it in the word: letter 1 after GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਮ (mammaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–2 (lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart line 952, commit de1e560; Apache-2.0) <https://github.com/codemanxdev/gnps_learning_hub/blob/de1e56014cb0caf7e56de2320681781cae6a7e41/lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart#L952>; letters 2 and 3 after GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਨ (nannaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–4 (lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart line 785, commit de1e560; Apache-2.0) <https://github.com/codemanxdev/gnps_learning_hub/blob/de1e56014cb0caf7e56de2320681781cae6a7e41/lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart#L785>. Each letter's own note on variation is printed with that letter's own strip. Letter 1 prints its headline split, with a gap above the body, and the cited source draws no separate bar for it: its own strokes, kept whole, draw the pieces of bar, and the shared headline does not cross the gap. It runs from the first to the last letter whose own headline stroke was taken off. The headline is then drawn once, left to right, along the word's printed bar. GNPS's tracing lesson draws every letter's headline FIRST, and each letter's own strip keeps that order; in a word this book draws it LAST instead, by convention: the order fluent writers are described as using, and the one it draws Devanagari words in, where native writers' consonant prototypes in HP Labs India's LipiTk 4.0 Devanagari recognizer draw the headline last in 82% of 2,706. The word-level order is not separately sourced: no reachable Gurmukhi recording shows a writer's headline timing in a word. It is a convention, not a rule.
